newsitem.title: UK: EMI seen little hurt by Musicland woes.
newsitem.headline: EMI seen little hurt by Musicland woes.

text.p: Analysts on Thursday played down the impact on EMI Group Plc of troubles at U.S. music retailer Musicland, said to have sent the stock sharply lower earlier in the session.
The stock was down 30p at 12.49 by 1240 GMT, after earlier dropping as much as 59p.

Dealers said the stock had been marked lower amid fears over the impact of troubles at Musicland, which said yesterday that it had asked record labels for concessions on payments while it seeks a cash injection. "All the talk today has been about Musicland," said one market-maker in EMI shares.
Yet analysts said EMI was relatively little exposed to the U.S. market and that the troubles at Musicland and other music retailers in the U.S. were already well known.
"This is not a new feature of the market. The consolidation of the U.S. music retail market is not new," said analyst Anthony de Larrinaga at Panmure Gordon.

Jason Crisp, analyst at SocGen, also said it was hard to see why EMI shares had reacted so negatively to the latest news from Musicland. "The fact that Musicland has been having problems has been known for some time," he said.

Traders and analysts said EMI may have been unsettled by results from WH Smith Plc SMWH.L on Wednesday, showing the company's music retail division Virgin Our Price fell into a 1.4 million stg loss on sales down two percent at 194 million stg.
And they said there was talk that a large line of EMI shares had been on offer in the market earlier in the session.
Yesterday industry sources said 750-store chain Musicland had asked major record labels including EMI to accept deferred payments with an option to covert the amounts due into equity in the company.
